  COVID-19 PUBLIC SERVICE ANNOUNCEMENT REGARDING MEETINGS OF
  THE INGLEWOOD CITY COUNCIL AND OTHER CITY LEGISLATIVE BODIES

Until further notice, meetings of the Inglewood City Council and other City legislative bodies will be conducted
pursuant to California Government Code section 54953(e), which allows the City to use teleconferencing for
members of the public to access a meeting and to address the legislative body via a call-in option.

CALL-IN OPTION

  1.Members of the public who wish to attend a public meeting and address the City Council or
  other legislative body during a public meeting must use the call-in option noted below:

  l  Members of the public may listen and make oral public comments telephonically by dialing:

  l  April 12, 2022 – Access Code: 6721843#
  l  April 19, 2022 – Access Code: 2738357#
  l  April 26, 2022 – Access Code: 6381037#

In the event of a disruption which prevents the City from broadcasting the meeting to the public using the call-in
option, or in the event of a disruption within the City’s control which prevents the public from offering public
   l  April 26, 2022 – Access Code: 6381037#

In the event of a disruption which prevents the City from broadcasting the meeting to the public using the call-in
option, or in the event of a disruption within the City’s control which prevents the public from offering public
comments using the call-in option, the City Council and other legislative body shall take no further action on
items appearing on the meeting agenda until public access to the meeting via the call- in option.

ALTERNATIVE METHODS

The City also provides alternative methods for members of the public to submit comments and/or to observe a
public meeting. The following alternative methods are provided to the public as a matter of convenience only
and the disruption in service to any alternative method does not preclude the City Council or other legislative
body from taking further action on an agenda item. In the event of a disruption to any alternative method below
members of the public should use the call-in option above.

  2. Submitting Comments Prior to Public Meeting: Members of the public may choose to submit
  comments electronically for consideration by the City Council or other City Legislative Body by sending
  them to the City Clerk/Secretary at athompson@cityofinglewood.org, and Deputy City Clerk
  at aallen@cityofinglewood.org. To ensure distribution to the members of the Legislative Body prior to
  consideration of the agenda, please submit comments prior to 8:00 a.m. the day of the meeting, and in
  the body of the email, please identify the agenda number or subject matter. Correspondence should
  indicate the meeting date and agenda item. Comments received after 8:00
  a.m. and prior to the close of the public hearings will be made part of the official public record of the
  meeting. Contact the Office of the City Clerk at 310-412-5280 with any questions.

  3. Viewing and Listening to the Meeting without Making Public Comments:

  l  On Spectrum Cable Channel 35 with audio and limited video. Please check with your cable provider
  for details.
  l  Live online through Facebook Live, with audio and limited video, at
  https://www.facebook.com/cityofinglewood/

  4.Public attendance at Gladys Waddingham Lecture Hall (located adjacent to the Main Library)
  to view meeting and make public comments via audio/video.

ACCESSIBILITY: If requested, the agenda and backup materials will be made available in appropriate
alternative formats to persons with a disability, as required by Section 202 of the Americans with Disabilities
Act of 1990 (42 U.S.C. Sec. 12132), and the federal rules and regulations adopted in implementation thereof.
Any person who requires a disability-related modification or accommodation, or translation services in order to
observe and/or offer public comment may request such reasonable modification, accommodation, or service by
contacting the Office of the City Clerk by telephone at 310- 412 -5280, FAX at 310 -412-5533, One
Manchester Boulevard, First Floor, Inglewood City Hall, Inglewood, CA 90301 or via email
to athompson@cityofinglewood.org and aallen@cityofinglewood.org no later than 24 hours prior to the
scheduled meeting.

Inglewood, California
  April 12, 2022

The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on Tuesday,
April 12, 2022, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.

Mayor Pro Tem Morales called the City Council into Closed Session at the hour of 1:00
p.m.

The City Clerk announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Mayor Pro Tem Morales, Council Members Dotson, Padilla, and
  Faulk; and
  Absent:  Mayor Butts.

City officials and personnel present for closed session were as follows:

  Aisha L. Thompson  City Clerk
  Ken Campos  City Attorney
  Angela Allen  Deputy City Clerk

PUBLIC COMMENTS REGARDING CLOSED SESSION ITEMS. Mayor Pro Tem
Morales inquired if there were any persons present who wished to address the City
Council on Closed Session Item Nos. CS-1, CS-2, CS-3, and CS-4.

There was no response.

Mayor Pro Tem Morales recessed the City Council at the hour of 1:01 p.m. for Closed
Session Items No. CS-1, CS-2, CS-3, and CS-4.

  *****************

Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called the
City Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, and Housing Authority at the
hour of 2:00 p.m.

The City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary announced the
presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present: Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman
  Butts, Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing
  Authority Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, and Faulk; and
  Absent: None.

City/Successor Agency/Housing Authority officials and personnel present were as
follows:

  Aisha L. Thompson  City Clerk/Secretary*
  Louis Atwell  Acting City Manager/ Acting Executive Director*
  Ken Campos  City Attorney/General Counsel*
  Angela Allen  Deputy City Clerk

* Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency, and Housing Authority.

PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS. Mayor/Successor Agency
Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts inquired if there were any persons present
who wished to address the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority on any
item on the Agendas.

City Clerk, Aisha L. Thompson reported that comments were received and passed out to
the City Council.
   April 12, 2022

142.9  PAYMENT OF WARRANTS AND BILLS. It was moved by Council Member/
  Successor Agency Member / Housing Authority Member Morales, and seconded by
  Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member Dotson that the
  demands presented to the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority dated April
  8, 2022, in the amount of $3,681,139.38 are hereby allowed, and the City
  Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary is hereby authorized to
  certify upon said registers that said demands are so approved. The motion was carried by
  the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing Authority Members
  Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  Mayor Butts announced that Agenda Item No. DR-1 was being pulled from the Agenda.

183&301  PUBLIC HEARING HELD – RESOLUTION NO. 22-71 ADOPTED –
  CERTIFICATION OF AN ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT REPORT (EA-EIR-
  2018-073), ADOPTION OF AN ENVIRONMENTAL MONITORING AND
  REPORTING PROGRAM IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE CALIFORNIA
  ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY ACT FOR THE INGLEWOOD TRANSIT
  CONNECTOR PROJECT; RESOLUTION 22-72 ADOPTED – AMENDMENTS
  TO THE LAND USE, CIRCULATION AND SAFETY ELEMENTS OF THE
  INGLEWOOOD GENERAL PLAN FOR THE INGLEWOOD TRANSIT
  CONNECTOR PROJECT; ORDINANCE NO. 22-08 INTRODUCED –
  APPROVAL OF ZONE CHANGE ZC-2022-001 TO ESTABLISH A
  TRANSPORTATION CORRIDOR OVERLAY ZONE; ORDINANCE NO. 22-09
  INTRODUCED – APPROVAL OF ZONING CODE AMENDMENT ZCA-2022-
  001 TO ESTABLISH A TRANSPORTATION CORRIDOR OVERLAY ZONE IN
  CHAPTER 12 (PLANNING AND ZONING) OF THE INGLEWOOD
  MUNICIPAL CODE; RESOLUTION NO. 22-73 ADOPTED – ADOPTION OF
  THE INGLEWOOD TRANSIT CONNECTOR DESIGN STANDARDS AND
  GUIDELINES. The City Clerk announced the next scheduled matter was a public
  hearing to consider multiple actions associated with the Inglewood Transit Connector
  (ITC) Project, notice had been given in the time, form, and manner as required by law, an
  affidavit was on file, and communications were received and passed out to Council.

  Mayor Butts ordered the communications received and filed.

  Louis Atwell, Assistant City Manager/Public Works Director, presented the Staff Report
  dated April 12, 2022.

  Lisa Trifiletti, Project Manager for the Inglewood Transit Connector (ITC), presented the
  City Council with an update on the project. She discussed the Inglewood Transit
  Connector Project, which aims to close the first last-mile gap to the Crenshaw Line and
  provide access to all city of Inglewood activity centers (The Forum, SoFi Stadium, and
  Clippers Arena) via the Metro Regional Rail System. She mentioned that the three
  stations will be located at Downtown Inglewood Market Street, across from the Forum,
  and across from the SoFi Stadium in Hollywood Park, near the upcoming Intuit Dome.
  She stated the project is an elevated guideway system, and it contains design standards
  and guidelines. Also, she emphasized the importance of partnering with small businesses
  and neighboring properties during construction, which included Vons Supermarket. She
  discussed the Draft Environmental Impact Report (EIR) and stated it was revised based
  on the community's input, which involved Inglewood Unified School District. Ms.
  Trifiletti reviewed the zoning overlay and determined it doesn't take away anyone's
  zoning land use rights. She further discussed the construction practice, which included a
  traffic management plan, a task force, a communications team that would work with local
  businesses to inform residents about detours and construction timing, and incorporate a
  twenty-four (24)-hour hotline.

  Additionally, she reported the ITC Project would provide transit access to the
  disadvantaged and low-income populations in the community. She also added that the
  Los Angeles Economic Development Corporation is also partnering with the project to

  2
 April 12, 2022

  hire 35% of local residents, 10% of disadvantaged businesses, and 20% of apprentices.
  Ms. Trifiletti reviewed the EIR timeline and discussed the comment letters that were
  received. Finally, she explained what would happen next with the ITC Project, which
  included the recommendations from the City Council.

  Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present who wished to address the City
  Council on the Public Hearing.

  Owen Smith, Miracle Theatre, spoke in favor of the ITC Project stating that he was
  looking forward to further connections with the community, and the ITC Project would
  be great. He also stated that the Miracle Theatre has been working hard to create a space
  that’s a cultural event theatre, and the ITC project would allow people to see downtown
  Inglewood.

  Franco Vega, CEO of the Right Way Foundation, and County Commissioner for Children
  and Families, 2nd District, spoke in favor of the project. The Right of Way Foundation
  has three facilities, and he gave background information on the services the program
  provides. He stated he has been fighting to get children from living in poverty after being
  emancipated from the foster care system. He also stated the City of Inglewood has a large
  percentage of foster youth and a project like the ITC Project would assist foster youth
  with obtaining employment once they are emancipated from the system.

  Mayor Butts closed the public comments portion at the hour of 2:20 p.m.

  Mayor Butts re-opened the public comments portion at the hour of 2:21 p.m.

  Ricardo Rosales, Midnight Mission, spoke in favor of the project stating it would help
  families in Inglewood who are experiencing homelessness. He stated residents have been
  able to take advantage of the jobs at SoFi Stadium, and they look forward to the jobs at
  the Intuit Dome. Furthermore, he felt the project would allow families to walk to the
  station and be able to take the people mover back and forth to work safely. Finally, he
  reiterated that the ITC Project would connect families and residents to the Metro Green
  Line.

  Mayor Butts closed the public comments portion at the hour of 2:24 p.m.

  Council Member Morales thanked Lisa Trifiletti for the ITC presentation. He stated this
  is an amazing development, that once was a dream and now it is reality. He also stated
  the project is a complete benefit to Market Street because it would be beneficial to the
  residents and Market Street would become better than it was.

  Council Member Padilla thanked Lisa Trifiletti and her team for putting together the EIR.
  He stated he appreciated the hard work done with community outreach, including local
  business owners. He also mentioned the positive impact the ITC Project would have on
  the traffic, which would alleviate people driving cars to events, and Market Street.
  Additionally, Council Member Padilla mentioned the 35% local hires of residents that
  would gain employment from the project. Finally, he reiterated that Inglewood was not
  losing Vons Supermarket.

  Council Member Morales left the dais at 2:26 p.m.

  Council Member Faulk thanked Lisa Trifiletti for the ITC presentation and explained
  how excited she was. She stated Ms. Trifiletti and her team did an outstanding job with
  keeping the community informed and presenting a presentation that’s understandable to
  the residents. Council Member Faulk also stated the project would be beneficial to the
  community by decreasing traffic congestion, bringing jobs to the community, improving
  Market street, and increased business production to the small business owners. Finally,
  she stated the City of Inglewood would have a monorail making the city one of the best
  in the world.

  Council Member Morales returned to the dais at 2:28 p.m.

  3
 April 12, 2022

  Lisa Trifiletti thanked Louis Atwell, Public Works Department Director, Christopher
  Jackson, Economic and Community Development Director, and Sharon Koike, Assistant
  Finance Director, and the rest of the staff who worked in partnership with the ITC
  Project.

  Council Member Dotson congratulated everyone that worked on the ITC Project. He
  stated he appreciates all the hard work that was put into this project, and wanted everyone
  to focus on the 35% local hire that would come to Inglewood.

  Mayor Butts stated that the proposal agnostic is the ultimate in technology, and the
  railing system would be above ground. He also stated the Council will decide later on
  what technology will be used. Finally, he emphasized that monorail is a generic term for
  elevated transportation.

  Mayor Butts re-opened the public comments portion at the hour of 2:31 p.m.

  Dexter Hall, Former President of the World Club of Inglewood, Chambers Board of
  Directors Member, spoke in favor of the project concerning its commitment to the
  minority and low-income population. He stated it would reduce residents commute time
  and create more economic opportunities. He also stated Inglewood residents would be
  more likely to utilize public transportation, and the ITC project would create thousands of
  jobs. Finally he added that the project would prioritize Inglewood residents.

  Matthew Newman, Board of Directors of the Inglewood Airport Area Chambers of
  Commerce, and Founder of All in Coworking of Inglewood, spoke in favor of the project
  stating it is important for him to re-emphasize what Council Member Padilla, and Council
  Member Faulk shared. He stated the project would bring more people to support small
  businesses that outline the city of Inglewood. Finally, he stated that the evolution must be
  embraced in order to remain competitive.

  Mayor Butts closed the public comments portion at the hour of 2:37 p.m.

  Mayor Butts provided clarity to the residents regarding the funding of the ITC project
  stating, “The city has accumulated over three-hundred and twenty million dollars in grant
  fund for the project. This project is going to be somewhere north of 1.2 billion. Our intent
  is to gather every dime of that from the state, county, and federal sources. The ITC
  Project is historic, one of a kind in the country, and shuttle ready. Now the project is
  going through the EIR, and Inglewood taxpayers will not finance it for construction."

  Mayor Butts mentioned for the record, to clarify and explain the updates to the project
  documents. He stated, the staff report and EIR Resolution had been updated to reflect that
  the project had no significant impacts and therefore no statement of overriding
  considerations were required for its approval. The hearing dates were updated to reflect
  the continuance of the public hearing. The GPA and zoning code amendments were
  updated to be consistent in format with the Planning Commission's unanimous support
  and recommendation. The design guidelines resolution was updated to make all
  documents consistent throughout the package of project approvals.

  Mayor Butts thanked Louis Atwell, Public Works Director, Sharon Kioke, Assistant
  Finance Director, the Planning staff, Chris Jackson, Economic and Community
  Development Director, Bernard McCrumby, Senior Planner, the legal team, and the
  consultant staff that helped make the project approval come to fruition.

  Additionally, Mayor Butts mentioned the first last-mile solution was critical and that it is
  a term of art in making sure you can take mass transit to get to where you really want to
  go. He stated, every project that the City of Inglewood has engaged in, such as the
  reconstruction of the Forum, the building of SoFi Stadium, and the soon to be the
  construction of the Intuit Dome, and the mission of the YOLA Building, all of which had
  30-35% local resident hire goals.

  4
 April 12, 2022

  Finally, Mayor Butts added that the critical missing component is how people can get to
  and from the region and that is where the ITC can change the future and bring economic
  security to the residents. He discussed the historical lack of public transportation that
  causes hardships for some of the city's most disadvantaged populations, including low-
  income residents. Furthermore, he stated the project would allow the people living in
  Inglewood the ability to travel throughout Los Angeles County for jobs, schools, and
  more. Finally, he discussed the estimated reduced carbon dioxide emissions, and air
  polluted-related illnesses that will not affect residents.

  The following callers spoke in favor of the ITC Project:

  Chris Hannon, Executive Secretary for Los Angeles/Orange Counties (LACO) Building
  Construction Trades Council.

  Caller (Name Unclear), LACO Building Trades.

  Jason Vogel, Owner of Career Expansion.

  Mayor Butts closed the public comment portion at the hour of 2:44 p.m.

  Following discussion, it was moved by Mayor Butts, and seconded by Council Member
  Morales that the City Council does hereby: 1) Adopt Resolution No. 22-71 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA, CERTIFYING AN ENVIRONMENTAL
  IMPACT REPORT, ADOPTING ENVIRONMENTAL MONITORING AND
  REPORTING PROGRAM IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE  CALIFORNIA
  ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY ACT FOR THE  INGLEWOOD  TRANSIT
  CONNECTOR PROJECT

  and 2) Adopt Resolution No. 22-72 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL ADOPTING AMENDMENTS
  TO THE LAND USE, CIRCULATION AND SAFETY ELEMENTS OF
  THE INGLEWOOD GENERAL PLAN FOR THE INGLEWOOD
  TRANSIT CONNECTOR PROJECT

  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  It was moved by Mayor Butts, and seconded by Council Member Morales that further
  reading be waived. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  Thereupon, Ordinance No. 22-08 entitled:

  A ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD,  CALIFORNIA, APPROVING ZONE CHANGE ZC-
  2021-001 TO ESTABLISH A TRANSPORTATION CORRIDOR OVERLAY ZONE

  was introduced by Mayor Butts, and seconded by Council Member Morales. The motion
  was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  It was moved by Mayor Butts, and seconded by Council Member Morales that further
  reading be waived. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  5
